archive_rebinding_scope: Only source catalog/split/import and preceding review references rebound to byte-identical preserved inputs. Original review retained; no decisions changed.
environment_scope: Previously executed native fresh-environment snapshots rebound by current exact SIF and artifact hashes; no new benchmark execution

explicit_distinctions.reason: Shared procurement entities, but invoice payment/discount decisions, supplier delivery-quality scores and PO-line matching have different outputs and central rules; shared data alone does not force one group.
Warehouse value aggregation, per-SKU depletion/lead-time forecasting and hourly capacity workload are distinct objectives and grains.

Hybrid decay on web sessions plus sales, five GA4 reporting models, funnel stages, session-quality scores and cart outreach share concepts but have different required submissions and source/linkage rules. No claim of unseen marketing domain.

Daily count/revenue, Sunday-week growth with explicit H1 scope, and monthly channel benchmark scorecards are distinct task targets; generic order aggregation is retained as a shared skill, not labeled unseen.
Category hierarchy profitability, product ABC/velocity, return-event timing/reasons and midpoint demand elasticity are distinct targets despite shared product/order entities.

Customer account ledger, unpaid/return/chargeback points, GL debits/credits, order header-line reconciliation, settlement FX and LIFO COGS have different governing rules and output grains; do not group merely as finance.

families.rationale: Shared GA sessions/events pipeline and daily date/channel/medium/campaign output with distinct sessions, converted-session purchase revenue and conversion rate. Paid-search and marketing instructions substantially repeat the core rules; email changes the fixed date window and normalization; multi-touch extends the output with five credit models and assist metrics. Keep together despite different windows and individual task defects.

Conservative component-overlap group: churn-cohorts and cohort-retention both require first-purchase monthly cohort retention/revenue; repeat-purchase extends the same cohort/bucket cumulative-revenue target. RFM segmentation-2 explicitly includes a monthly cohort-retention output, connecting the RFM variants. CLV and customer-order tasks share customer order count/spend/first-last-date/value-segmentation components; advanced CLV includes inter-order gaps, churn and cohort outputs, connecting order-interval metrics and weekly churn warning. Forecasts, thresholds, filters, data layers and customer universes differ. This intentionally broad 12-task group limits reuse across splits without asserting identical answers; it does not group unrelated retail tasks merely for sharing orders.

Overlapping order processing/delivery and carrier/fulfillment metrics. The analytics task includes shipment/carrier and order lifecycle outputs also used conceptually by SLA and order-type summaries. Group conservatively; shipment/month versus warehouse/day versus order-type grains and their filters remain distinct.

All require deduplicated within-order product/SKU pairs and support/confidence/lift association metrics. Temporal, segment, hierarchy and bundle extensions differ. Basket composition remains separate because it classifies basket size/value transitions rather than product-pair association rules.

Product performance explicitly combines revenue-contribution ABC classification and product sales velocity, linking the specialized ABC and velocity tasks. Different filters, windows, return handling and score definitions remain recorded; no claim of identical final tables.

Both explicitly request monthly channel revenue/AOV outputs; one adds growth/market benchmarks and the other fact-dimension profit/discount/margin with required view/tags. Group conservatively despite different sales sources and channel representations.

Both identify a customer first-order acquisition channel and summarize customer/order/revenue quality by channel. Sales channel IDs versus UTM-derived marketing attribution and their filters differ. Distinct from per-session GA4 attribution.

Both construct marketing spend/revenue and payback metrics. Campaign-day cumulative waterfall versus monthly channel/new-customer segments and 90-day payback differ. Conservatively keep both within one split; MMM econometric baseline/adstock/saturation remains a different task.

Related fraud/velocity anomaly objectives across orders and payments, with different required flags and input score sources. Conservative fraud family; customer unpaid/return/chargeback point scoring remains a separate output objective.

limitations: Shared retail warehouse is explicitly recorded; this is not unseen-warehouse generalization.
Conservative groups include related but non-equivalent tasks; narrower future grouping requires a separately versioned review.
Moving historical train tasks to test cannot make them a clean holdout for old checkpoints.
Instruction-level family review does not establish gold correctness, actual solvability or verifier coverage.
Full catalog metadata migration and evidence identity review are required before activating a frozen split.
proposed_assignment_policy: Keep groups intact; if any member was v3 test, assign the entire group to test. Otherwise train. No rewards/validation outcomes used.
